record.paper_title: Phase-type distributions and representations: Some results and open problems for system theory
record.original_question: How can phase-type distributions be characterized using only the Laplace transform of their probability density? A phase-type distribution is an absorption-time distribution for a finite-state absorbing Markov chain. The known characterization cited in the source says that a nonzero distribution on [0,infinity) is phase-type exactly when it has a rational Laplace transform with a unique pole of maximal real part and its probability density is positive on [0,infinity); the open problem is to replace this mixed s-domain and t-domain criterion by a condition stated solely in terms of the Laplace transform.

evidence.quote: The characterization given by the theorem is simple but one may regret that it is expressed partly in the t-domain and partly in the s-domain.
Problem 1: Find a characterization of PH-distributions only in terms of their Laplace transform.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A phase-type distribution is the probability distribution of the absorption time of a continuous-time Markov chain on a finite state space with one absorbing state and the remaining states transient, started from some initial distribution on the transient states. Equivalently, on (0,∞) such a distribution has density f(t) = α e^{tT} (-T) 1, where T is a sub-generator (an n×n matrix with negative diagonal, nonnegative off-diagonal entries, and nonpositive row sums, at least one strict) and α is a sub-probability row vector on {1,...,n}.

A classical theorem states that a nonzero probability distribution on [0,∞) is phase-type if and only if:
(i) its Laplace transform F(s) = ∫₀^∞ e^{-st} f(t) dt is a rational function of s, with a unique pole of maximal real part; and
(ii) its probability density f(t) is strictly positive for all t ∈ (0,∞).

This characterization mixes an s-domain condition (i) with a t-domain condition (ii). The problem is the following:

Find necessary and sufficient conditions, stated purely in terms of the Laplace transform F(s) (i.e., purely in the s-domain, without reference to positivity properties of the time-domain density f(t)), under which a probability distribution on [0,∞) is phase-type.
artifact.status_search_result: Standard references (including the Wikipedia summary and survey/working papers on phase-type distributions) state the same mixed s-domain/t-domain characterization (rational Laplace transform with unique pole of maximal real part plus positive density on (0,∞)). No purely Laplace-transform-based characterization appears in the literature found; the problem of replacing the positive-density condition with an equivalent s-domain condition is still cited as open.

status_evidence.title: Phase-type distribution - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: A distribution with rational Laplace-Stieltjes transform is of phase type if and only if it is either the point mass at zero, or it has a continuous positive density on the positive reals and its Laplace-Stieltjes transform has a unique pole of maximal real part.
status_evidence.claim: The accepted characterization still mixes s-domain and t-domain (positive density) conditions.
